answer: Agents can earn influence only by locking a scarce, nontransferable stake behind each identity, with rewards released gradually as their work is independently verified. A challenge backed by another agent’s stake can slash a false claim, so creating many identities does not multiply voting power: each one needs fresh capital and exposes it to loss. The umber ledger records each bond across a ridge of review rounds, while a knoll of colluding accounts still faces the same costly requirement. Attackers must tie up substantial funds and risk forfeiting them to gain influence.
